newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE fails to agree on Albania force - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: OSCE fails to agree on Albania force - diplomats.

text.p: A meeting of the permanent council of Europe's top security body broke up on Wednesday without agreement on an international security force to oversee aid operations in Albania, diplomatic sources said.

The sources said the 54-member Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) failed to agree on whether a United Nations mandate was necessary to allow a security force to operate in the crisis-torn Balkan nation.
"The sticking point was the United Nations mandate," a Western diplomat said.
The sources said the council would reconvene at a future date, yet to be agreed upon.

Diplomats said earlier on Wednesday there had been broad consensus that former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, the OSCE's peace envoy to Albania, should head the operation and that the only stumbling block to an agreement was an Albanian government request for more time to look at the draft decision.
They said the OSCE was looking at a multinational force "of the willing" that would probably include Italy, Spain, Greece, France and several others.
